title: Two Sum
statement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in any order.

examples.explanation: The same element cannot be reused, so [0, 0] is invalid.

optimalComplexity: O(n) time, O(n) space — one pass with a hash map from value to index.
rubric: Reaches the single-pass hash map solution, not the O(n^2) double loop.
Stores value -> index, and checks for the complement BEFORE inserting the current element.
Does not reuse the same index twice.
Can state the time and space complexity when asked.
followUps: What if the array were already sorted? (two pointers, O(1) extra space)
What if there could be multiple valid pairs and you had to return all of them?
What if the array were too large to fit in memory?
